title: Isolation and functional analysis of peridroplet mitochondria from murine brown adipose tissue
protocol: Euthanize mice one-by-one using isoflurane and secondary cervical dislocation as approved by your institutional animal care and use committee in compliance with US Public Health Service Regulation.
Handle isoflurane in a fume hood to avoid exposure.
Exsanguinate mice by cardiac puncture using a syringe with a 23G needle.
Dissect interscapular brown adipose tissue (BAT) from 6 male 12-week-old C57BL/6J mice and place in a 6-well plate or petri dish containing ice-cold PBS.
Separate BAT from connective tissue, muscle, and white adipose tissue using surgical scissors and forceps, preferably with the aid of a dissection microscope.
Weigh pooled BAT tissue (480 mg minimum).
Mince pooled BAT tissue into approximately 2 mm pieces using scissors or razors.
Re-suspend tissue pieces in MIB + BSA at a ratio of 10:1 (volume: weight).
Disrupt tissue with 9–10 strokes in an ice-cold glass/Teflon Dounce homogenizer until the solution appears homogeneous and smooth.
Transfer the homogenate into an ice-cold 50 mL Falcon tube.
Centrifuge at 900 × g for 10 minutes at 4°C using a centrifuge with a swinging bucket rotor.
Carefully pour the supernatant into a new ice-cold falcon tube.
Use a cell strainer to prevent debris or loose fat from mixing with the CM fraction.
Scrape the fat layer, which is fraction 1, into a second clean ice-cold 50 mL tube.
Resuspend fraction 1 in 4 mL of MIB + BSA buffer.
Alternatively, use a P1000 micropipette with 1/3 of its tip cut to collect fraction 1.
Cutting 1/3 of the pipette tip increases its bore size and prevents clogging when aspirating the fat layer.
Ensure sufficient tissue is homogenized to generate a compact and floating fat layer on the surface of the homogenate.
Save 1 μL of fraction 1 for peridroplet mitochondria imaging as quality control assessment.
Discard the original 50 mL tube containing pelleted unbroken cells, nuclei, and debris.
Repeat low-speed centrifugation on fraction 1 re-suspended in 4 mL of MIB + BSA.
Repeat low-speed centrifugation on fraction 2 in a new tube to further eliminate debris.
Transfer clean fraction 1 and fraction 2 to 2 mL Eppendorf tubes.
Centrifuge at 10,000 × g for 10 min at 4°C using a microfuge.
Discard the lipid layer and supernatants generated after centrifuging Fractions 1 and 2.
Use a P1000 pipette to physically scrape the lipid layer.
Gently evacuate residual lipids before removing supernatant.
Save at least 1 μL of the discarded lipid layer for quality control measurements.
Re-suspend pellets in 200 μL MIB + BSA.
Transfer re-suspended pellets to clean 1.5 mL tubes.
Repeat high-speed centrifugation step to wash residual lipids and non-mitochondrial contents with MIB + BSA.
Remove supernatant after the second high-speed centrifugation.
Preserve washed pellets with mitochondria.
Perform additional centrifugation steps until no lipid layer is observed.
Gently re-suspend mitochondrial pellets by pipetting up and down in ice-cold MIB without BSA.
Determine protein concentration by BCA assay (Thermo).
Re-suspend pellet in MIB aiming for a concentration of ∼10 μg/μL (1:2–1:3 volume pellet: buffer).
Use MIB without BSA for protein determination.
Load the cartridge with 15 μL MAS + ADP in port A.
Load the cartridge with 16.6 μL MAS + oligomycin in port B.
Load the cartridge with 18.5 μL MAS + FCCP in port C.
Load the cartridge with 20.5 μL MAS + antimycin A in Port D.
Plate mitochondria with ADP.
Add 15 μL MAS + oligomycin in port A.
Add 16.6 μL MAS + FCCP in port B.
Add 18.5 μL MAS + antimycin A in port C.
Add 20.5 μL MAS + TMPD/Ascorbate in Port D to determine maximal complex IV activity.
Load the protocol prepared the day before the assay.
Press start.
Place the utility plate containing the hydrated sensor cartridge into the XF96 analyzer.
Calibrate oxygen and pH sensors for 30 minutes.
Load mitochondria into the XF96 cell culture microplate during calibration.
Generate a master mix with sufficient volume for at least triplicate measures (3 wells) for each mitochondrial fuel.
Prepare each well to contain 2–4 μg of mitochondria in 20 μL MAS + substrate to be assessed.
Ensure each master mix contains at least a total of 60 μL with 6-12 μg of mitochondria per substrate.
Load 20 μL of each master mix into individual wells using a P20 pipette.
Centrifuge the plate at 2,000 × g for 5 minutes at 4°C to sediment mitochondria.
Load mitochondria in the center of the well.
Turn OFF centrifuge brake to allow the rotor to reduce speed gradually.
Add 115 μL MAS + GDP + substrate using a multichannel pipette at a 45° angle to each chamber well.
Warm the Seahorse plate with mitochondria in a 37°C incubator for 5 minutes before loading into the XF96 Analyzer.
Replace the utility plate with the Seahorse plate loaded with mitochondria and start the assay.
Export point-to-point oxygen consumption rates (OCRs) from Seahorse instrument for individual wells.
Check that the oxygen tension traces are linear in each measurement as a quality control parameter.
Using Microsoft Excel, perform the calculations described with the OCR values measured in each individual well.
Subtract the OCR under Antimycin A from other values to obtain the OCR that corresponds to mitochondrial respiratory function.
State 2: Subtract the minimal OCR value following antimycin A injection from the maximal OCR value at the start of the assay.
State 3: Subtract the minimal OCR value following antimycin A injection from the maximal OCR value following ADP injection.
State 4o: Subtract the minimal OCR value following antimycin A injection from the minimal OCR value following oligomycin injection.
Maximal: Subtract the minimal OCR value following antimycin A injection from the maximal OCR value following FCCP injection.
Measure respiratory control ratio as a quantitative measure of mitochondrial inner membrane damage.
Assess mitochondria and lipid droplet content by fluorescence microscopy.
Combine 1 μL of non-stripped fat layer with 1 μL Imaging solution A.
Combine 1 μL of stripped fat layer with 1 μL Imaging solution A.
Combine 1 μL of isolated PDMs with 1 μL Imaging solution A.
Place 1 μL of each sample-Imaging solution A mix on a #1.5H coverglass.
Cover the coverglass with an additional coverglass.
Place the coverglass on a confocal microscope stage.
Image BODIPY using 488 nm laser for excitation and collect fluorescence emission at 500–550 nm.
Use a separate track to image MitoTracker with 633 nm excitation.
Collect emission at 650–700 nm.
Use a 20× lens for low-magnification imaging of LD content.
Combine 1–10 μg isolated mitochondria and boil at 95 °C for 5 min.
Run an SDS gel as specified by the gel apparatus manufacturer.
Transfer the SDS gel according to the manufacturer's instructions.
Probe for the relative content of mitochondrial markers such as TOMM20 or VDAC.
Quantify the mitochondrial markers per microgram of protein loaded.
Combine 1 μL of isolated mitochondria with 1 μL of Imaging solution B.
Place 1 μL of the mitochondria-solution B mix on a #1.5H coverglass.
Cover the mixture with an additional coverglass.
Place the coverglass on the microscope stage.
Image MitoTracker green using a 488 nm laser excitation and a 500–550 nm emission.
Image MitoTracker red with a 633 nm excitation and a 650–700 nm emission.
